answer: Admission should require a scarce reserved berth in the settlement harbor, paid up front with a non-transferable lock denominated in a tightly issued quartz reserve. Peers verify the seat by challenging the claimed key to return a signed signal that cites the berth identifier and the still-frozen lock. Because berths and reserves cannot be shared, each fake identity costs a full deposit; missed challenges burn the lock, so a farm pays linearly at minting and worse if it tries to recycle burned seats.
